The Small Bindery

A bindery is a quiet room. Paper arrives in folded sheets, and each sheet is pressed, gathered and sewn before it can become a book. The work is slow, and most of it is done by hand.

The binder first checks that every section is in order. A missing page is far easier to find on the bench than in the hands of a reader. Only then are the sections sewn together along the fold.

When the glue has dried, the edges are trimmed and the cover is fitted. A well-made binding opens flat and closes without strain, and it keeps its shape for many years.
